P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Not needed in the usual sense: the US dollar has been Ecuador's official currency since 2000, so ordinary local accounts are already in dollars. A 2023 Monetary Board resolution requires all transactions and their accounting records in Ecuador to be expressed in dollars (trade.gov). Watch the 5% capital exit tax (ISD) on money sent abroad (trade.gov; exceptions exist).

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: RIMPE (Régimen Simplificado para Emprendedores y Negocios Populares): 'Negocio Popular' covers individuals with gross income up to USD 20,000 a year, who file one annual income-tax return. 'Emprendedor' covers gross income above USD 20,000 and up to USD 300,000 (Expreso). The SRI recategorises taxpayers by prior-year income; in 2026 about 14,000 people moved from Negocio Popular to Emprendedor and about 56,000 left RIMPE for the general regime (Vistazo, citing the SRI). Check your current category on your RUC. Whether your specific activity is excluded from RIMPE was not checked.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw in local currency'). (6) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
